$comment: U17: slide the three QSPI escape vias east, vacating the crystal guard lane.
U16 moved U2 2.5 mm east but deliberately left these vias at x 166.642/166.670/
166.764. The crystal guard has to reach x = 166.450 for X1's 0.5 mm eastward move
(the fix plan 002 walked back), and a 0.254 guard there has its east edge at
166.577 -- overlapping all three via west edges. So the lane is still blocked and
U16 alone does not enable the crystal fix.
What U16 DID buy is room east of them: U2's west pads went 167.590 -> 170.090, so
the corridor that plan 002 measured at 0.96 mm (keepout edge 166.129 to pads
167.090) is now 3.46 mm. These vias move into that space.
IO3 IS THE AWKWARD ONE. /QSPI_IO1 runs the bottom layer at y = 107.750 and IO3's
via sits at y = 107.841, 0.091 mm away. Sliding IO3 east along its own y drives it
into IO1 -- the exact short that revision 2 of U16 hit. So IO3 escapes NORTH-east
to y = 108.480 instead, threading between IO1's run below and the /+3V3 via above.
That gap is genuinely tight (0.303 mm to IO1, 0.174 mm to the +3V3 via), so the
+3V3 via and its local stub are ripped here and left for the router; +3V3 is not
held and re-routing it is cheaper than threading a 0.17 mm gap.
After this the guard lane is clear from 166.129 east to 167.700, and the crystal
fix recorded under the crystal group in kicad_netclass.json becomes attemptable
for the first time since it was walked back.
REVISION 2: IO0 IS DROPPED AND ITS VIA STAYS AT x=166.642.
Extending IO0 east on Inner1 crosses QSPI_CLK's existing Inner1 wall -- the
vertical at x=167.272 spanning y 105.055-105.817 -- and routing south around it
runs into the /GND Inner1 diagonal from (164.943,102.031) to (168.753,105.841)
instead. Inner1 is full through that window.
CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY: the guard lane is NOT fully cleared. A 0.254 guard at
x=166.450 has its east edge at 166.577 and IO0's via west edge is 166.342, so they
still overlap. CLK and IO3 moving east is real progress but it does not on its own
enable the crystal fix. Finishing this needs U1's east escape re-planned as a whole
rather than more incremental via moves -- pins 20-26 all escape into a ~2 mm gap
between U1 and X1, and that congestion is the actual root cause.
